subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which type of business ownership is owned by its shareholders but cannot sell shares to the general public?
questions.explain: A private limited company (Ltd) is owned by shareholders but its shares cannot be sold to the public.

questions.q: A common business objective for a brand-new start-up is most likely to be:
questions.explain: Survival is a key short-term objective for new businesses, which often face high failure rates early on.

questions.q: Which statement about a sole trader is correct?
options: They have unlimited liability for business debts
questions.explain: A sole trader has unlimited liability, meaning personal assets are at risk if the business cannot pay its debts.

questions.q: What does 'limited liability' mean for the owners of a private limited company (Ltd)?
options: Owners are personally responsible for all business debts
Owners can lose only the amount they invested
The business has limited time to operate
questions.explain: Limited liability means shareholders can only lose the money they invested, not their personal assets.

questions.q: According to Maslow, which is a lower-level (basic) need?
options: Physiological needs such as pay for food and shelter
questions.explain: In Maslow's hierarchy, physiological needs (e.g. basic pay) are at the bottom and must be met first.

questions.q: A business in the public sector is one that is:
options: Always run to make maximum profit
Owned and run by the government
questions.explain: The public sector is owned and controlled by the government, usually to provide public services.

questions.q: A financial method of motivation is:
questions.explain: A bonus is a financial reward, so it is a financial method of motivation.

questions.q: What is the difference between a merger and a takeover?
options: A merger is two firms agreeing to join; a takeover is one firm buying control of another
A takeover is two firms agreeing to join as equals
They are exactly the same thing
A merger always fails; a takeover always succeeds
questions.explain: In a merger two firms agree to combine; in a takeover one firm gains control of another, sometimes against its wishes.

questions.q: Which is an example of a non-financial method of motivation?
questions.explain: Job rotation and added responsibility motivate without extra pay, so they are non-financial methods.

Watching online videos at home only
questions.explain: On-the-job training takes place at the workplace while the employee carries out the job.

Always done away from the workplace
questions.explain: Induction training introduces new employees to the business, their role and procedures.

The leader making all decisions alone
questions.explain: A democratic leader consults and involves employees when making decisions.
